## Overview

Minecraft Backup wraps the [`itzg/minecraft-server`](https://docker-minecraft-server.readthedocs.io/en/latest/) image with a custom entrypoint that treats the world folder as a Git repository. The world is restored from GitHub when the container starts, committed and pushed at a fixed interval while people play, and backed up one last time after the server stops cleanly, so a world can always be recovered, moved to another machine or rolled back to an earlier commit.

* **Periodic backups**: a Git commit every `PERIODIC_INTERVAL` minutes, created only when something changed.
* **Consistent snapshots**: automatic saving is paused (`save-off` / `save-all flush`) while files are staged.
* **Graceful shutdown**: the server stops first, then the final backup is committed and pushed.
* **Safe credentials**: the GitHub token stays in memory, never in the remote URL, the repository config or the logs.
* **Any Git remote**: GitHub by default, or GitLab, Gitea or a bare repository through `GIT_REMOTE_URL`.
* **Compatible with the official image**: every `itzg/minecraft-server` variable still works.

## Quick start

```bash
git clone https://github.com/danieltorquatof/minecraft-backup.git
cd minecraft-backup
cp .env.example .env   # set GITHUB_USER, GITHUB_TOKEN and REPO_NAME
docker compose up -d --build
```

The [README](https://github.com/danieltorquatof/minecraft-backup#readme) covers the token permissions, every variable and how to restore an older backup.

| 2025-12-04 | **Initial release**: periodic Git backups to GitHub, restore on startup and backup on shutdown. |
